messages.text:
"Mobile landscape top-down firefighter rescue game Mr. Rescue: Extinguish Protocol. Pixel art (red helmet, yellow suit). Full phone screen, no black bars.

Dual joysticks: left=move, right=aim+fire (appears on touch). Bottom button switches Water/Foam/Cryo/CO2. Show current type + Ready/Cooldown. Touch only.

Hold right joystick to spray. Cooldown (10-15s) starts only on release. Correct type extinguishes matching enemies with clear effect. Wrong type does little.

Enemy looks: Water=bright orange/yellow flames, Foam=dark oily/magma, Cryo=pale blue frostfire, CO2=purple/green gas.

Rescue civilians only when close. Throw/drop only near windows or main door. Heat rises near fire. Fire spreads. Score on rescues. Multiple rooms. Update score/rescue count on success.

Collisions: player, enemies, civilians stop at walls/furniture. Player flashes red + takes damage on enemy/fire contact. Has health. Zero health = Crew Down. Sprite stays upright (no weird tilt).

Synergies, heat risk/reward, civilian variety, room objectives, power-ups, living fire, style grade, light rogue-lite upgrades.

Enemy patrols: circular guards, doorway blockers, sweepers, figure-8, leash, chase when carrying civilian.

Temp messages vanish in 2-3s. UI: heat, extinguisher status, health, score, civilians, grade. End of floor needs most civilians rescued. No debug overlays. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
s=Path('index.html').read_text()
Path('/tmp/opencode/game.js').write_text(re.search(r'<script>(.*?)</script>',s,re.S).group(1))
PY
node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js

content.text:
Built the game in `index.html` as a full-screen, touch-controlled pixel-art rescue game.

- Left stick moves; hold and drag the right stick to aim and spray. Releasing starts the extinguisher cooldown. Tap the bottom button to cycle Water, Foam, Cryo, and CO₂.
- Rescue civilians by getting close, then escort them to the main exit. Rescue at least 3 of 4 to clear a floor and choose an upgrade.
- Added matching elemental enemies and fires, spreading flames, heat and health risk, patrol behaviors, power-ups, score, rescue count, and grade.

Assumption: the main exit is the extraction point for every room. JavaScript syntax validation passed. I couldn’t verify the game in a browser or capture a screenshot because Chromium isn’t installed in the environment.
